policy.text: Collision coverage pays for sudden physical damage when the insured car collides with another vehicle or object, subject to a $500 deductible.
Collision coverage excludes intentional damage and ordinary mechanical breakdown.

claimant_facts.incident: The insured car struck the rear of another car while approaching a traffic light.
claimant_facts.damage: The front bumper and hood are dented; the repair estimate is $2,800.
claimant_facts.other_facts: The insured driver was driving, no one was injured, and the damage was accidental.

decision.reason: The accidental collision damage is covered subject to the $500 deductible, and the supplied clauses impose no collision-date requirement.

policy.text: Comprehensive coverage pays for sudden accidental damage to the insured car from events such as fire, theft, hail, or falling objects.
Damage caused by floodwater or other surface-water inundation is excluded, even when the car was parked and the event was accidental.

claimant_facts.incident: The car was parked in an underground garage during a heavy rainstorm; floodwater rose around it.
claimant_facts.damage: Water reached the floorboards, the car will not start, and the repair estimate is $6,200.
claimant_facts.other_facts: There was no collision, fire, or intentional act.

decision.reason: The reported floodwater damage is expressly excluded even when the car was parked and the flooding was accidental.

policy.text: Comprehensive coverage pays for malicious damage by another person to a stationary insured car, including vandalism, subject to a $250 deductible.
This coverage does not apply when the damage was caused by the policyholder or an authorized driver.

claimant_facts.incident: The car was parked overnight in a public lot; the next morning the owner found a scratched door and broken side window.
claimant_facts.other_facts: The owner did not cause the damage, no authorized driver had the car, and a police report was filed.

decision.reason: The damage is documented, but malicious damage by another person has not been established, and the policyholder or authorized-driver exclusion does not apply.

policy.text: Personal property theft away from the residence is covered up to $1,000 for each item, subject to a $100 deductible.
For theft away from the residence, the insured must file a police report and provide its reference number.

claimant_facts.insured_item: A fictional renter's personal property policy

claimant_facts.damage: The laptop has not been recovered.
claimant_facts.other_facts: The owner filed a police report the same afternoon; reference number FIC-2048.

decision.reason: The $850 laptop theft away from home is covered subject to the $100 deductible, and the police report requirement is satisfied; neither supplied clause requires the theft date.

tasks.title: Late notice after a water leak

policy.text: Sudden accidental water damage from a burst household pipe is covered.
The insured should report a loss within 30 days after discovering it.
When notice arrives more than 30 days after discovery, an adjuster must review whether the delay materially prejudiced the investigation; late notice alone does not determine coverage.

claimant_facts.insured_item: A fictional renter's personal property policy
claimant_facts.incident: A supply pipe burst and leaked onto the kitchen floor while the renter was away.
claimant_facts.damage: The renter discovered water damage to personal property after returning home.
claimant_facts.other_facts: The renter reported the loss 44 days after discovery because they were hospitalized for most of that period; the amount and cause of damage still need inspection.

decision.reason: The burst-pipe loss is potentially covered, but an adjuster must determine whether the 44-day reporting delay materially prejudiced the investigation.
